CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFLOOP

CFLOOP repeats the code between its start and end tags. The attributes you give it decide the kind of loop: INDEX/FROM/TO counts, CONDITION repeats while an expression is true, QUERY walks the rows of a query, LIST walks the elements of a list, and COLLECTION walks the keys of a structure.

Category

Flow control

Syntax

<!--- index loop --->
<CFLOOP INDEX="index_name"
    FROM="start"
    TO="end"
    STEP="increment">
  HTML and CFML
</CFLOOP>

<!--- conditional loop --->
<CFLOOP CONDITION="expression">
  HTML and CFML
</CFLOOP>

<!--- query loop --->
<CFLOOP QUERY="query_name"
    STARTROW="row_num"
    ENDROW="row_num">
  HTML and CFML
</CFLOOP>

<!--- list loop --->
<CFLOOP INDEX="index_name"
    LIST="list_items"
    DELIMITERS="item_delimiter">
  HTML and CFML
</CFLOOP>

<!--- collection loop --->
<CFLOOP COLLECTION="#structure#"
    ITEM="key_name">
  HTML and CFML
</CFLOOP>

Attributes

INDEX
Required for index and list loops. Variable that receives the counter (index loop) or the current list element (list loop).
FROM
Required for index loops. First value of the counter.
TO
Required for index loops. Last value of the counter. The loop ends when the counter passes it.
STEP
Optional, default "1". Amount added to the counter after each pass. Use a negative step to count down; 0 is not allowed.
CONDITION
Required for conditional loops. Expression tested before each pass; the loop runs while it is true. Write it without pound signs so it is evaluated afresh every time.
QUERY
Required for query loops. Name of the query to loop over.
STARTROW
Optional, default "1". First row of a query loop.
ENDROW
Optional. Last row of a query loop. Defaults to the last row of the query.
LIST
Required for list loops. The list to loop over, usually written with pound signs, for example LIST="#Form.FieldNames#".
DELIMITERS
Optional, default ",". Characters that separate list elements. Each character is a delimiter on its own, and empty elements are skipped.
COLLECTION
Required for collection loops. The structure to loop over, written with pound signs: COLLECTION="#Prefs#".
ITEM
Required for collection loops. Variable that receives the name of the current key.

Usage

Inside a query loop the columns of the current row can be used without the query name, and query_name.CurrentRow tells you where you are. Unlike CFOUTPUT QUERY=, a query loop can be nested inside CFOUTPUT and inside other query loops, and it has no GROUP attribute.

A collection loop hands you the key names, not the values; read the value with Prefs[key] or StructFind. The keys arrive in no particular order. ColdFusion on Windows can also loop over COM collections; KoldFusion loops over structures only.

Use CFBREAK to leave any kind of loop early. A conditional loop whose condition never turns false runs until the request timeout set in the Administrator stops it, so make sure something in the body changes the condition.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFOUTPUT>
<P><B>Index loop</B> (FROM 10 TO 1 STEP -3):
<CFLOOP INDEX="i" FROM="10" TO="1" STEP="-3"> #i#</CFLOOP></P>

<P><B>Conditional loop</B> (double it until it passes 1000):
<CFSET n = 1>
<CFLOOP CONDITION="n LT 1000"><CFSET n = n * 2> #n#</CFLOOP></P>

<P><B>List loop</B> (delimiters ";" and "|"):
<CFLOOP INDEX="Browser" LIST="Netscape 4.7;Internet Explorer 5|Opera 3.6;Lynx" DELIMITERS=";|">
  [#Browser#]</CFLOOP></P>

<P><B>Collection loop</B>:
<CFSET Modem = StructNew()>
<CFSET Modem.Speed = "56K">
<CFSET Modem.Standard = "V.90">
<CFSET Modem.Port = "COM2">
<CFLOOP COLLECTION="#Modem#" ITEM="Key"> #Key#=#Modem[Key]#</CFLOOP></P>
</CFOUTPUT>

<P><B>Query loop</B> (rows 2 to 4 of Departments):</P>
<CFQUERY NAME="Depts" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
SELECT Dept_Name, Location FROM Departments ORDER BY Dept_ID
</CFQUERY>
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<CFLOOP QUERY="Depts" STARTROW="2" ENDROW="4">
  <CFOUTPUT><TR><TD>#Depts.CurrentRow#</TD><TD>#Dept_Name#</TD><TD>#Location#</TD></TR></CFOUTPUT>
</CFLOOP>
</TABLE>
